purpose: Unapproved branding direction, not a screenshot of implemented software
prompt:
Create exactly one high-fidelity desktop application branding and UI concept for TENET, a local read-only inspector of coding-agent policy decisions. Landscape 1536x1024, edge-to-edge real software layout. This is concept 3, 'Wayfinder'. Translate the confidence and clarity of international airport signage into an exceptionally designed developer tool. Not an airport website, no flights, buildings, photographs, marketing slogan or illustration. Saturated sign-yellow #F3CB16 owns a full-height left navigation region around 23% of the frame and the header, very dark sign-black #151714 owns one broad outcome band, white and cool-light-gray #E8E9E4 are quiet evidence reading surfaces. Bold highly legible humanist sans reminiscent of Frutiger, strict sign-panel alignments, squared white-on-black pictogram tiles, purposeful large words, a robust TENET wordmark. No bevels, glowing cyberpunk, gradients, decorative dashed maps, fake metrics, little card dashboard or rounded pill soup. Yellow is the BRAND and NAVIGATION color, not a warning color. Red stop and green PASS are limited semantic colors.

Composition: a shallow yellow top strip with TENET wordmark at far left and 'Local archive / Read-only', 'Refresh archive' at the far right. Below it a full-height yellow navigation rail about 300px wide, with session selector 'tenet-observe', a large useful heading 'Recent calls', and five compact command rows arranged like a navigable sign index. The selected 'Shell command / Would block' row is a BLACK inset band with WHITE text and a white directional arrow locked to its left edge. Other rows in black type on yellow: 'Edit file / Would allow', 'Edit file / Block', 'Shell command / Would allow', 'Edit file / Would ask for approval'. Never show 'Approve' controls. Each row is clearly a call record, not a destination or gate in an airport.

The main workspace is broad and tightly composed, separated from the rail by a fine black rule. Its first major region is a charcoal-black outcome sign spanning the full width, roughly 220px tall. On the left, an outlined RED stop octagon and enormous WHITE words 'Would block', small associated field label 'TENET decision'. On the right, separated by a thin pale vertical rule, WHITE 'Ran', small field label 'Actual execution'. Under the two outcomes, a readable sentence across the sign 'The call ran. Observe mode records decisions without enforcing them.' Give the decision typographic authority without making the whole screen scream. One dominant focal band, everything else quiet.

Under this black band a clean white action strip headed 'Shell command', with exact dark monospace command 'git status --short && git diff -- README.md && git diff --cached --stat'. Then a larger white evidence reading area, ample internal alignment, fine horizontal separators instead of individual cards. Heading 'Why this decision'. Sentence 'Evidence confidence was below the required threshold.' The rule 'Never send any email without confirmation.' with a small GREEN 'PASS' outcome and 'Rule at line 5'. Below, a broad exact meter labeled 'Evidence confidence', fill from zero to 0.85 in dark neutral ink, strong vertical threshold mark at 0.9, scale ends '0' and '1', clearly aligned labels 'Recorded 0.85' and 'Required 0.9'. Do not color insufficient confidence green. Beneath it: 'PASS is not a reported violation. The evidence-confidence check did not pass.' At the bottom, four compact expansion rows with square pictogram buttons and right arrows: 'Submitted questions', 'Shared evidence', 'All rules', 'Recording details'. Tiny footer 'Synthetic preview data'. Controls must read as navigation and disclosures, not enforcement or approval. The final image must feel like an unmistakable branded product, all navigation and states consistently using this signage grammar, while the precise archived explanation remains easy to read. One polished screen, all text legible. No arbitrary numeric safety scores, no invented claims or extra capabilities.
reviewNotes: Branding reference only. Meter geometry requires exact implementation rather than copying generated pixels. Yellow remains a navigation color, not a warning state.
